The story is a fresh, original piece of writing that actively avoids romantic and dramatic clichés. Instead of relying on overused tropes—such as a terrifying, melodramatic near-death experience when the tide comes in, or a sweeping, cinematic declaration of love—the narrative stays grounded in dry humor and specific, quirky details (like a kayak held together with smiley-face packing tape and a borrowed, ill-fitting wetsuit). The narrator even explicitly subverts cliché romantic expressions, noting, "I should tell you that my heart did not hammer. That would be a lie." Furthermore, the characters' professions (a choreographer and a marine biologist) and their understated, practical approach to their expiring summer fling feel unique and authentic rather than predictable.
